edition: Global Injustice Investigation, revised desk report, 3 November 2026
method: Revised-report URLs were requested on 3 November 2026. A sentence is published only when the opened page supports it. The first edition log is superseded for what this edition states.

entries.claim: DOJ case page: 4 March 2015 findings that Ferguson police and court practices systematically violate the First, Fourth, and Fourteenth Amendments, with a revenue focus and race bias.
Inquiry reports page: Volume 1, 8 July 2025, human impact and redress.
Volume 1 PDF cover: ordered printed 8 July 2025.
BSR assessment undertaken May to September 2018. It cannot predate 2017.
Rwanda government PDF: notice of arbitration on 24 November 2025 under the migration treaty. Not the 5 August 2024 parliamentary answer.
World Bank: 1.3 billion adults still lack accounts, alongside growth in account ownership.
BSR, 22 September 2022: did not identify intentional bias; identified unintentional bias and greater over-enforcement of Arabic content.
Meta, same day: unintentional impact on Palestinian and Arab communities.
Federal Reserve, 22 October 2020: $154 million fine of Goldman Sachs for 1MDB oversight failures. Not the $2.9 billion resolution.
NAO: does not evaluate value for money of the COVID contracts; sample had insufficient documentation in specific cases.
CPJ: 330 journalists imprisoned as of 1 December 2025, down from 384 in 2024.
CPJ, 25 February 2026: 129 press members killed in 2025; database changes. Replaces 130.
Citizen Lab validated Pegasus infections in four iTunes backups. Not every leaked number.
Citizen Lab, 12 June 2025: forensic confirmation involving Paragon iOS spyware and journalists devices. No method repeated.
Amnesty, 19 July 2021: 50,000 numbers of potential targets, including Jamal Khashoggi family. Not confirmed infections.
CJEU, 18 June 2020, C-78/18: Hungary funding restrictions breach EU law, including Charter articles on private life, personal data, and association.
CIVICUS 2025: severe attack in 122 of 198 jurisdictions; 15 downgrades and 3 upgrades. Ratings, not a closure census.
Charity Commission, 11 June 2019: Oxfam GB safeguarding mismanagement and an official warning.
Oxfam accepted the findings, apologised, and describes tripled safeguarding investment. Not independent proof of beneficiary safety.
KFF June 2022: 41 percent of US adults have some medical or dental debt under a broad definition.
ILO: forced labour in the private economy generates US$236 billion in illegal profits a year, up 37 percent since 2014.
World Bank, 23 June 2022: estimated 70 percent of 10-year-olds in low- and middle-income countries cannot understand a simple text.
UN Goal 16 2026: homicide rate 5.9 per 100,000 in 2015 and 5.1 in 2024.
IC3 2025 PDF: 1,008,597 complaints, $20.877 billion losses, up 26 percent; cyber-enabled fraud $17.697 billion.
OHCHR page for the 20 February 2026 report on trafficking into cyber-scam operations.
INTERPOL, 7 June 2023: warning that people are trafficked to work in online scam centres.
NAO press release: WannaCry NHS impact could have been prevented by basic IT security practice.
Microsoft, 20 July 2024: CrowdStrike update affected an estimated 8.5 million Windows devices. Not an intrusion.
OECD 2024 insights on the 2023 adult-skills survey: reading text, numbers, and complex problems. Not an AI-literacy census.
Abstract: 1,818 dark-pattern instances on about 11,000 shopping websites. Shopping sites only. No method reproduced.
World Inequality Report 2026: top 10 percent own three-quarters of global wealth; bottom half holds 2 percent.
BIS, 4 November 2021: NSO Group and Candiru added to the Entity List.
Treasury, 5 March 2024: OFAC designated two individuals and five Intellexa-related entities. Not the 2021 Entity List action.
Judgment document 810, 12 November 2025: $4,447,190, of which $444,719 compensatory and $4,002,471 punitive. Injunction dates stated in the PDF.
Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre. The only fraud-reporting link. Not a statistical source.
Revised report: parliamentary answer that the Rwanda partnership was finished on 5 August 2024. HTTP 403. The date is not a finding.
Revised report: A.R.E. v. Greece and G.R.J. in the 2025 annual report. The PDF did not yield readable text. Not a finding.
Revised report: 1 December 2016 Haiti cholera remarks. The URL did not return the statement. Not a finding.
Revised report: December 2016 Odebrecht plea. The page returned a bot check, not the announcement. Not a finding.
Revised report: Goldman Sachs 1MDB resolution above $2.9 billion. The page returned a bot check. The $2.9 billion figure is not used.
Revised report: 2026 OECD lobbying and revolving-door chapter. HTTP 403. Not a finding.
Revised report: 31 July 2018 International Development Committee report. HTTP 403. Not used as replication of the Oxfam inquiry.
Revised report: US wage-and-hour recovery tables. HTTP 403. No recovery total is stated.
Revised report: May 2024 Kenya flood-eviction reporting. HTTP 403. Not a finding.
Revised report: May 2024 testimony that a Change Healthcare portal lacked multifactor authentication. HTTP 403. Not a finding.
Revised report: September 2022 dark-patterns staff report. HTTP 404. Not a finding and not a fraud-reporting link.
Revised report: richest tenth holds 85.4 percent of net financial wealth. HTTP 403. Not a finding.
Revised report: global financial-wealth concentration easing. HTTP 403. Not a finding.
Revised report: Ninth Circuit docket 26-874 shows 2026 briefing. HTTP 403. Appeal status is not stated.
Revised report: 5 January 2026 Federal Register page 329 removes three individuals. The retrieved file did not contain those names. Removals are not a finding.
Revised report: Italian official positions on Paragon surveillance. HTTP 403. Not summarised.
Revised report cited the FBI file-repository copy of the 2025 IC3 report. That URL returned 403. The same report was opened at ic3.gov and is the published source.
Earlier unqualified 130 deaths in 2025. Replaced by the 25 February 2026 release reporting 129, with a database-change warning.

The revised report cites Amnesty's forensic methodology. The page opened. It is a how-to for catching the spyware, so it is not published. The four-backup conclusion is taken from Citizen Lab's peer review instead.
Two earlier cross-dossier sentences, that missing records are usually held by powerful actors and that hidden top-level harm exceeds hidden household harm, are withdrawn. They are not established.
